scenes.text: TWO FRIENDS BOTH CLAIM THEY'VE CHOSEN THE BIGGER SHARE OF THE SAME SIZED CHOCOLATE BAR HOW COULD A PICTURE SETTLE THIS DELICIOUS DISAGREEMENT
TODAY WE'RE LEARNING TO COMPARE AND ORDER FRACTIONS SO WE CAN EXPLAIN WHICH AMOUNT IS GREATER SMALLER OR EQUAL
YOU'LL COMPARE SHARES FAIRLY USING HOLES OF THE SAME SIZE
YOU USE A PICTURE OR EQUIVALENT FRACTIONS TO EXPLAIN YOUR CHOICE RATHER THAN GUESSING FROM THE NUMBERS
AND YOU PUT FRACTIONS IN ORDER BY FINDING THEIR POSITIONS ON A NUMBER LINE
FIRST CHOOSE ONE WHOLE ITS PARTS MUST BE EQUAL IN SIZE THE OUTLINE OF THE MODEL SHOWS THE ENTIRE WHOLE NOT JUST THE COLORED SHARE
HERE THREE EQUAL PARTS ARE CHOSEN OUT OF FOUR THE TOP NUMBER THE NUMERATOR COUNTS CHOSEN PARTS THE BOTTOM NUMBER THE DENOMINATOR TELLS HOW MANY EQUAL PARTS MAKE THE WHOLE
A FRACTION STARTS WITH EQUAL PARTS HERE ONE WHOLE IS DIVIDED INTO FOUR EQUAL PIECES
SHADE THREE PIECES THE NUMERATOR THREE COUNTS THE SHADED PARTS THE DENOMINATOR FOUR COUNTS THE EQUAL PARTS IN THE WHOLE
A STRIP SHOWS THE SAME AMOUNT THREE OR FOUR EQUAL LENGTHS ARE SHADED THE PICTURE CHANGES BUT THE VALUE STAYS THE SAME
LOOK AT THESE TWO EQUAL SIZED HOLES WHICH HAS THE GREATER COLOURED SHARE COUNT THE QUARRISIZED PIECES BEFORE YOU DECIDE
WHEN DENOMINATORS MATCH THE PIECES HAVE THE SAME SIZE THREE QUARTERS IS GREATER THAN TWO QUARTERS BECAUSE THREE PIECES ARE MORE THAN TWO
WE CAN COUNT THESE PIECES DIRECTLY BECAUSE THEIR SIZE IS MATCH WITH THE SAME DENOMINATOR AND EQUAL SIZED HOLES MORE CHOSEN PARTS MEANS MORE OF THE WHOLE
NOW COMPARE ONE THIRD AND ONE SIXTH THESE HOLES ARE THE SAME LENGTH BUT THE SIXTH ARE SMALLER PIECES
SO ONE THIRD IS GREATER THAN ONE SIXTH A BIGGER DENOMINATOR DOES NOT ALWAYS MEAN A BIGGER FRACTION
IT CAN BE TEMPTING TO CHOOSE THE FRACTION WITH THE BIGGER DENOMINATOR BUT DIVIDING THE SAME WHOLE INTO MORE PIECES MAKES EACH PIECE SMALLER NOT BIGGER
NOW THE PIECES HAVE DIFFERENT SIZES PREDICT WHETHER THREE QUARTERS OR ONE HALF IS GREATER COULD YOU DESCRIBE THE HALF USING QUARTERS
RETURN TO THREE QUARTERS AND ONE HALF SPLIT EACH HALF INTO TWO EQUAL PIECES ONE HALF BECOMES TWO QUARTERS
ONLY THE DIVISIONS HAVE CHANGED THE HALF STILL COVERS EXACTLY THE SAME LENGTH TWO QUARTERS AND ONE HALF ARE EQUIVALENT NAMES FOR THAT AMOUNT
NOW THE PARTS MATCH THREE QUARTERS IS GREATER THAN TWO QUARTERS SO THREE QUARTERS IS GREATER THAN ONE HALF
A NUMBER LINE SHOWS FRACTION SIZE AS DISTANCE FROM ZERO DIVIDE THE DISTANCE FROM ZERO TO ONE INTO FOUR EQUAL INTERVALS
ONE QUARTER IS ONE INTERVAL FROM ZERO ONE HALF IS TWO INTERVALS AND THREE QUARTERS IS THREE INTERVALS
READ FROM LEFT TO RIGHT TO ORDER THEM FROM SMALLEST TO LARGEST ONE QUARTER ONE HALF THEN THREE QUARTERS
WHICH IS GREATER FIVE EIGHTHS OR THREE EIGHTHS
FIVE EIGHTHS IS GREATER THE SAME SIZED PARTS ARE BEING COUNTED

OUR GOAL WAS TO COMPARE AND ORDER FRACTIONS YOU CAN COMPARE EQUAL PARTS EXPLAIN A FAIR COMPARISON AND READ A NUMBER LINE WHICH MODEL WILL HELP YOU EXPLAIN YOUR NEXT ANSWER TRY THE PRACTICE ON MATHEMATIC
